title: CosmoAtlas

basics.tagline: Interactive Cosmic Knowledge Graph & AI Cosmology Platform

listing.shortDescription: A full-stack scientific platform for exploring cosmic hierarchies, astronomical scale, cosmological theories, guided journeys, and AI-powered scientific reasoning.
listing.fullDescription: CosmoAtlas maps the universe from Earth and planetary systems through galaxies, superclusters, cosmic phenomena, and theoretical geometries. Its interactive graph, canvas visualizations, scale navigator, cosmic timeline, guided journeys, dossier generator, and Claude-powered Atlas copilot turn complex cosmology into an explorable knowledge system with deterministic fallbacks when AI services are unavailable.

cover.imageAlt: CosmoAtlas interactive cosmic knowledge graph landing screen showing connected astronomical entities, cosmic scale relationships, Claude AI assistance, and educational universe exploration, AI cosmology software services in the USA, UK, India, and Australia

closing.clientOverview: CosmoAtlas is designed for astrophysics students, science communicators, educators, amateur astronomers, space enthusiasts, and theoretical physics researchers who need more than static astronomy articles or an unstructured AI chat window.
closing.conclusion: CosmoAtlas combines a secure server-side Claude proxy, structured JSON responses, an interactive cosmic graph, procedural 2D canvas visuals, guided journeys, and local astrophysical fallbacks. The result is an educational research surface that makes cosmic scale, hierarchy, chronology, and theoretical models easier to explore without exposing API credentials to the browser.

challenge.summary: Astronomy learners and researchers had to combine static articles, specialist simulation tools, and unstructured AI chat to understand cosmic hierarchy, scale, traversals, and theoretical models together.

points.title: Disconnected cosmic taxonomy
points.description: It was difficult to see how local structures such as Earth and the Solar System nest inside the Milky Way, Laniakea, and the Observable Universe.

points.title: No relational traversal
points.description: Static search could describe objects but could not guide users through a meaningful physical path from one cosmic entity to another.

points.title: AI scientific rigor
points.description: A general-purpose chatbot can blur the distinction between observed structures, supported models, theoretical geometries, and speculative ideas.

points.title: Client-side API exposure
points.description: AI prototypes often place provider credentials in browser code, creating avoidable security and operational risks.

solution.summary: CosmoAtlas unifies graph topology, scale, chronology, theory comparison, guided traversal, and secure AI reasoning behind one responsive application architecture.

points.title: Structured cosmic graph
points.description: Typed astronomical entities and relationships provide exact hierarchy, adjacency, physical metadata, scientific consensus, and mystery context.

points.title: Agentic Atlas actions
points.description: The AI copilot returns typed actions such as NAVIGATE, HIGHLIGHT_PATH, COMPARE, and SCALE_TO instead of unstructured chat alone.

points.title: Exponential visualization
points.description: The scale navigator and canvas camera make astronomical magnitude understandable through interactive zoom, targeting, and orbital context.

points.title: Grounded scientific output
points.description: Schema-enforced explanations, reports, comparisons, and local fallbacks preserve consistent output shapes and scientific status labels.

points.title: Secure fallback architecture
points.description: Express proxies Claude model calls server-side while deterministic datasets preserve usability during missing-key, network, or rate-limit failures.
